\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}

\title{Practical Identity-Based Encryption for Constrained Devices}
\author{N.~Haddad and E.~Moreau}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Related Work}
Two lines of work are most relevant to our study. First, Boneh and
Franklin introduced the first fully functional identity-based encryption
(IBE) scheme built from bilinear pairings on elliptic curves,
establishing that practical IBE is achievable from standard
number-theoretic assumptions. Their construction remains the reference
point for essentially all deployed IBE systems, but its pairing
operations are expensive on microcontrollers with tight energy budgets.

Second, Gentry presented the first construction of fully homomorphic
encryption based on ideal lattices, demonstrating that arbitrary
computation can be carried out over encrypted data. Although homomorphic
encryption solves a different problem than IBE, Gentry's lattice
techniques have inspired a family of lattice-based IBE schemes whose
operations are far cheaper on constrained hardware and which are believed
to resist quantum attacks.

Our implementation draws on both lines: we keep the Boneh--Franklin key
architecture for compatibility with existing key servers, while replacing
pairing-heavy operations with lattice-based alternatives wherever the
security model permits.

\end{document}
